passages.text: Now when news of this reached all the kings west of the Jordan—those in the hill country, the foothills, and all along the coast of the Great Sea toward Lebanon (the Hittites, Amorites, Canaanites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites)— they came together to wage war against Joshua and Israel.
passages.sermon:
All the kings west of the Jordan heard the news.
These kings ruled in the hill country, the foothills, and along the coast of the Great Sea toward Lebanon.
These kings included the Hittites, Amorites, Canaanites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites.
They gathered together.
They united to fight against Joshua and Israel.
They spoke and acted as one.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֣י כִשְׁמֹ֣עַ כָּֽל־ הַמְּלָכִ֡ים אֲשֶׁר֩ בְּעֵ֨בֶר הַיַּרְדֵּ֜ן בָּהָ֣ר וּבַשְּׁפֵלָ֗ה וּבְכֹל֙ ח֚וֹף הַיָּ֣ם הַגָּד֔וֹל אֶל־ מ֖וּל הַלְּבָנ֑וֹן הַֽחִתִּי֙ וְהָ֣אֱמֹרִ֔י הַֽכְּנַעֲנִי֙ הַפְּרִזִּ֔י הַחִוִּ֖י וְהַיְבוּסִֽי׃ וַיִּֽתְקַבְּצ֣וּ יַחְדָּ֔ו לְהִלָּחֵ֥ם עִם־ יְהוֹשֻׁ֖עַ וְעִם־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל פֶּ֖ה אֶחָֽד׃פ

passages.text: But the people of Gibeon, having heard what Joshua had done to Jericho and Ai, acted deceptively and set out as envoys, carrying on their donkeys worn-out sacks and old wineskins, cracked and mended.
passages.sermon:
The people of Gibeon heard what Joshua did to Jericho and Ai.
Joshua was the leader of Israel.
He defeated Jericho and Ai.
The people of Gibeon decided to act with deception.
They planned to trick Joshua and Israel.
They set out as envoys.
They carried worn-out sacks on their donkeys.
They took old wineskins.
The wineskins were cracked and mended.
passages.original: וְיֹשְׁבֵ֨י גִבְע֜וֹן שָׁמְע֗וּ אֵת֩ אֲשֶׁ֨ר עָשָׂ֧ה יְהוֹשֻׁ֛עַ לִֽירִיח֖וֹ וְלָעָֽי׃ וַיַּעֲשׂ֤וּ גַם־ הֵ֙מָּה֙ בְּעָרְמָ֔ה וַיֵּלְכ֖וּ וַיִּצְטַיָּ֑רוּ וַיִּקְח֞וּ שַׂקִּ֤ים בָּלִים֙ לַחֲמ֣וֹרֵיהֶ֔ם וְנֹאד֥וֹת יַ֙יִן֙ בָּלִ֔ים וּמְבֻקָּעִ֖ים וּמְצֹרָרִֽים׃

passages.text: They put worn, patched sandals on their feet and threadbare clothing on their bodies, and their whole supply of bread was dry and moldy.
passages.sermon:
The people of Gibeon wanted to deceive Joshua and Israel.
They put old sandals on their feet.
These sandals were worn and patched.
They wore clothes that were old and threadbare.
All the bread they brought was dry.
The bread was also moldy.
passages.original: וּנְעָל֨וֹת בָּל֤וֹת וּמְטֻלָּאוֹת֙ בְּרַגְלֵיהֶ֔ם וּשְׂלָמ֥וֹת בָּל֖וֹת עֲלֵיהֶ֑ם וְכֹל֙ לֶ֣חֶם צֵידָ֔ם יָבֵ֖שׁ הָיָ֥ה נִקֻּדִֽים׃

passages.text: They went to Joshua in the camp at Gilgal and said to him and the men of Israel, “We have come from a distant land; please make a treaty with us.”
passages.sermon:
The people of Gibeon heard what Joshua did to Jericho and Ai.
They decided to act deceptively.
They traveled as envoys to the Israelites.
They went to Joshua.
Joshua was in the camp at Gilgal.
The Gibeonites spoke to Joshua and to the men of Israel.
They said, “We have come from a distant land.
Please make a treaty with us.”
passages.original: וַיֵּלְכ֧וּ אֶל־ יְהוֹשֻׁ֛עַ אֶל־ הַֽמַּחֲנֶ֖ה הַגִּלְגָּ֑ל וַיֹּאמְר֨וּ אֵלָ֜יו וְאֶל־ אִ֣ישׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל מֵאֶ֤רֶץ רְחוֹקָה֙ בָּ֔אנוּ וְעַתָּ֖ה כִּרְתוּ־ לָ֥נוּ בְרִֽית׃

passages.text: But the men of Israel said to the Hivites, “Perhaps you dwell near us. How can we make a treaty with you?”
passages.sermon:
The men of Israel spoke to the Hivites.
The Hivites were a group of people living in the land near Israel.
The men of Israel said, “Perhaps you live close to us.”
They asked, “How can we make a treaty with you?”
passages.original: וַיֹּאמְרוּ אִֽישׁ־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל אֶל־ הַחִוִּ֑י אוּלַ֗י בְּקִרְבִּי֙ אַתָּ֣ה יוֹשֵׁ֔ב וְאֵ֖יךְ אֶכְרוֹת לְךָ֥ בְרִֽית׃

passages.text: “We are your servants,” they said to Joshua. Then Joshua asked them, “Who are you and where have you come from?”
passages.sermon:
The men spoke to Joshua.
They said, “We are your servants.”
Joshua replied to them.
He asked, “Who are you?”
He also asked, “Where have you come from?”
passages.original: וַיֹּאמְר֥וּ אֶל־ יְהוֹשֻׁ֖עַ עֲבָדֶ֣יךָ אֲנָ֑חְנוּ וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֲלֵהֶ֧ם יְהוֹשֻׁ֛עַ מִ֥י אַתֶּ֖ם וּמֵאַ֥יִן תָּבֹֽאוּ׃

passages.text: “Your servants have come from a very distant land,” they replied, “because of the fame of the LORD your God. For we have heard the reports about Him: all that He did in Egypt, and all that He did to the two kings of the Amorites beyond the Jordan—Sihon king of Heshbon and Og king of Bashan, who reigned in Ashtaroth.
passages.sermon:
The Hivites spoke to Joshua.
They said, “We are your servants.
We have come from a very distant land.
We came because of the name of the LORD your God.
We heard about the LORD.
We heard all that He did in Egypt.
We also heard what He did to the two kings of the Amorites.
These kings lived beyond the Jordan River.
One king was Sihon, king of Heshbon.
The other king was Og, king of Bashan.
Og ruled in Ashtaroth.”
passages.original: וַיֹּאמְר֣וּ אֵלָ֗יו מֵאֶ֨רֶץ רְחוֹקָ֤ה מְאֹד֙ בָּ֣אוּ עֲבָדֶ֔יךָ לְשֵׁ֖ם יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֑יךָ כִּֽי־ שָׁמַ֣עְנוּ שָׁמְע֔וֹ וְאֵ֛ת כָּל־ אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשָׂ֖ה בְּמִצְרָֽיִם׃ וְאֵ֣ת׀ כָּל־ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֗ה לִשְׁנֵי֙ מַלְכֵ֣י הָאֱמֹרִ֔י אֲשֶׁ֖ר בְּעֵ֣בֶר הַיַּרְדֵּ֑ן לְסִיחוֹן֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ חֶשְׁבּ֔וֹן וּלְע֥וֹג מֶֽלֶךְ־ הַבָּשָׁ֖ן אֲשֶׁ֥ר בְּעַשְׁתָּרֽוֹת׃

passages.text: So the elders and inhabitants of our land told us, ‘Take provisions for your journey; go to meet them and say to them: We are your servants. Please make a treaty with us.’
passages.sermon:
The elders of our land spoke to us.
All the people who live in our land also spoke to us.
They said, “Take food with you for the journey.”
They said, “Go to meet the people of Israel.”
They told us, “Say to them, ‘We are your servants.’”
They told us, “Now make a treaty with us.”
passages.original: וַיֹּאמְר֣וּ אֵלֵ֡ינוּ זְֽקֵינֵינוּ֩ וְכָל־ יֹשְׁבֵ֨י אַרְצֵ֜נוּ לֵאמֹ֗ר קְח֨וּ בְיֶדְכֶ֤ם צֵידָה֙ לַדֶּ֔רֶךְ וּלְכ֖וּ לִקְרָאתָ֑ם וַאֲמַרְתֶּ֤ם אֲלֵיהֶם֙ עַבְדֵיכֶ֣ם אֲנַ֔חְנוּ וְעַתָּ֖ה כִּרְתוּ־ לָ֥נוּ בְרִֽית׃

passages.text: This bread of ours was warm when we packed it at home on the day we left to come to you. But take a look, it is now dry and moldy.
passages.sermon:
The Gibeonites spoke to Joshua and the Israelites.
They said, "This is our bread."
We packed this bread at home.
The bread was warm when we packed it.
We packed it on the day we left our homes.
We left our homes to come to you.
Now, look at the bread.
The bread is dry.
The bread is moldy.
passages.original: זֶ֣ה׀ לַחְמֵ֗נוּ חָ֞ם הִצְטַיַּ֤דְנוּ אֹתוֹ֙ מִבָּ֣תֵּ֔ינוּ בְּי֥וֹם צֵאתֵ֖נוּ לָלֶ֣כֶת אֲלֵיכֶ֑ם וְעַתָּה֙ הִנֵּ֣ה יָבֵ֔שׁ וְהָיָ֖ה נִקֻּדִֽים׃

passages.text: These wineskins were new when we filled them, but look, they are cracked. And these clothes and sandals are worn out from our very long journey.”
passages.sermon:
The Gibeonites spoke to Joshua and the Israelites.
They showed their wineskins.
They said, “We filled these wineskins when they were new.
Now, look at them.
They are cracked.
They showed their clothes and sandals.
They said, “These clothes and sandals are worn out.
Our journey was very long.
That is why our clothes and sandals are worn out.”
passages.original: וְאֵ֨לֶּה נֹאד֤וֹת הַיַּ֙יִן֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר מִלֵּ֣אנוּ חֲדָשִׁ֔ים וְהִנֵּ֖ה הִתְבַּקָּ֑עוּ וְאֵ֤לֶּה שַׂלְמוֹתֵ֙ינוּ֙ וּנְעָלֵ֔ינוּ בָּל֕וּ מֵרֹ֥ב הַדֶּ֖רֶךְ מְאֹֽד׃

passages.text: Then the men of Israel sampled their provisions, but did not seek the counsel of the LORD.
passages.sermon: The men of Israel took some of the food from the visitors.\r\nThey did not ask the LORD what to do.
passages.original: וַיִּקְח֥וּ הָֽאֲנָשִׁ֖ים מִצֵּידָ֑ם וְאֶת־ פִּ֥י יְהוָ֖ה לֹ֥א שָׁאָֽלוּ׃

passages.text: And Joshua made a treaty of peace with them to let them live, and the leaders of the congregation swore an oath to them.
passages.sermon:
Joshua was the leader of Israel.
Joshua made peace with the Gibeonites.
Joshua made a treaty with the Gibeonites.
The treaty allowed the Gibeonites to live.
The leaders of the congregation of Israel swore an oath to the Gibeonites.
passages.original: וַיַּ֨עַשׂ לָהֶ֤ם יְהוֹשֻׁ֙עַ֙ שָׁל֔וֹם וַיִּכְרֹ֥ת לָהֶ֛ם בְּרִ֖ית לְחַיּוֹתָ֑ם וַיִּשָּׁבְע֣וּ לָהֶ֔ם נְשִׂיאֵ֖י הָעֵדָֽה׃

passages.text: Three days after they had made the treaty with the Gibeonites, the Israelites learned that they were neighbors, living among them.
passages.sermon:
The Israelites made a treaty with the Gibeonites.
Three days passed after they made this treaty.
The Israelites then learned new information.
They discovered that the Gibeonites were their neighbors.
The Gibeonites lived among the Israelites.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֗י מִקְצֵה֙ שְׁלֹ֣שֶׁת יָמִ֔ים אַחֲרֵ֕י אֲשֶׁר־ כָּרְת֥וּ לָהֶ֖ם בְּרִ֑ית וַֽיִּשְׁמְע֗וּ כִּי־ קְרֹבִ֥ים הֵם֙ אֵלָ֔יו וּבְקִרְבּ֖וֹ הֵ֥ם יֹשְׁבִֽים׃

passages.text: So the Israelites set out and on the third day arrived at their cities—Gibeon, Chephirah, Beeroth, and Kiriath-jearim.
passages.sermon:
The Israelites were God's chosen people.
The Israelites traveled together.
They set out on a journey.
They traveled for three days.
On the third day, they reached the cities of the Gibeonites.
These cities were Gibeon, Chephirah, Beeroth, and Kiriath-jearim.
The Israelites arrived at these four cities.
passages.original: וַיִּסְע֣וּ בְנֵֽי־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל וַיָּבֹ֛אוּ אֶל־ עָרֵיהֶ֖ם בַּיּ֣וֹם הַשְּׁלִישִׁ֑י וְעָרֵיהֶם֙ גִּבְע֣וֹן וְהַכְּפִירָ֔ה וּבְאֵר֖וֹת וְקִרְיַ֥ת יְעָרִֽים׃

passages.text: But the Israelites did not attack them, because the leaders of the congregation had sworn an oath to them by the LORD, the God of Israel. And the whole congregation grumbled against the leaders.
passages.sermon:
The Israelites did not attack the Gibeonites.
The leaders of the congregation had sworn an oath to the Gibeonites.
They swore this oath by the LORD, the God of Israel.
The whole congregation grumbled against the leaders.
passages.original: וְלֹ֤א הִכּוּם֙ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל כִּֽי־ נִשְׁבְּע֤וּ לָהֶם֙ נְשִׂיאֵ֣י הָֽעֵדָ֔ה בַּֽיהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיִּלֹּ֥נוּ כָל־ הָעֵדָ֖ה עַל־ הַנְּשִׂיאִֽים׃

passages.text: All the leaders answered, “We have sworn an oath to them by the LORD, the God of Israel, and now we cannot touch them.
passages.sermon:
The leaders of Israel spoke to all the people.
They said, “We have made a promise to these people.
We swore this oath by the LORD.
The LORD is the God of Israel.
Now we cannot harm them.
We must keep our promise.”
passages.original: וַיֹּאמְר֤וּ כָל־ הַנְּשִׂיאִים֙ אֶל־ כָּל־ הָ֣עֵדָ֔ה אֲנַ֙חְנוּ֙ נִשְׁבַּ֣עְנוּ לָהֶ֔ם בַּֽיהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וְעַתָּ֕ה לֹ֥א נוּכַ֖ל לִנְגֹּ֥עַ בָּהֶֽם׃

passages.text: This is how we will treat them: We will let them live, so that no wrath will fall on us because of the oath we swore to them.”
passages.sermon:
The leaders of Israel had sworn an oath to the Gibeonites by the LORD, the God of Israel.
The leaders said, "We will do this to them."
"We will let them live."
We do this so that no wrath will come upon us.
We do not want God's anger because of the oath we swore to them.
passages.original: זֹ֛את נַעֲשֶׂ֥ה לָהֶ֖ם וְהַחֲיֵ֣ה אוֹתָ֑ם וְלֹֽא־ יִֽהְיֶ֤ה עָלֵ֙ינוּ֙ קֶ֔צֶף עַל־ הַשְּׁבוּעָ֖ה אֲשֶׁר־ נִשְׁבַּ֥עְנוּ לָהֶֽם׃

passages.text: They continued, “Let them live, but let them be woodcutters and water carriers for the whole congregation.” So the leaders kept their promise.
passages.sermon:
The leaders of Israel spoke to the Gibeonites.
The leaders said, "Let the Gibeonites live."
The leaders gave the Gibeonites a task.
The Gibeonites must cut wood for the people of Israel.
The Gibeonites must carry water for the people of Israel.
The Gibeonites must serve the whole congregation.
The leaders did as they had promised.
passages.original: וַיֹּאמְר֧וּ אֲלֵיהֶ֛ם הַנְּשִׂיאִ֖ים יִֽחְי֑וּ וַ֠יִּֽהְיוּ חֹטְבֵ֨י עֵצִ֤ים וְשֹֽׁאֲבֵי־ מַ֙יִם֙ לְכָל־ הָ֣עֵדָ֔ה כַּאֲשֶׁ֛ר דִּבְּר֥וּ לָהֶ֖ם הַנְּשִׂיאִֽים׃

passages.text: Then Joshua summoned the Gibeonites and said, “Why did you deceive us by telling us you live far away from us, when in fact you live among us?
passages.sermon:
Joshua was the leader of Israel.
Joshua called the Gibeonites to him.
Joshua spoke to the Gibeonites.
Joshua said, “Why did you deceive us?
You told us, ‘We live very far from you.’
But you actually live among us.”
passages.original: וַיִּקְרָ֤א לָהֶם֙ יְהוֹשֻׁ֔עַ וַיְדַבֵּ֥ר אֲלֵיהֶ֖ם לֵאמֹ֑ר לָמָּה֩ רִמִּיתֶ֨ם אֹתָ֜נוּ לֵאמֹ֗ר רְחוֹקִ֨ים אֲנַ֤חְנוּ מִכֶּם֙ מְאֹ֔ד וְאַתֶּ֖ם בְּקִרְבֵּ֥נוּ יֹשְׁבִֽים׃

passages.text: Now therefore you are under a curse and will perpetually serve as woodcutters and water carriers for the house of my God.”
passages.sermon:
Joshua spoke to the Gibeonites.
Joshua said, “You are now under a curse.
You will always be servants.
You will cut wood for the house of my God.
You will carry water for the house of my God.
You and your descendants will do this forever.”
passages.original: וְעַתָּ֖ה אֲרוּרִ֣ים אַתֶּ֑ם וְלֹֽא־ יִכָּרֵ֨ת מִכֶּ֜ם עֶ֗בֶד וְחֹטְבֵ֥י עֵצִ֛ים וְשֹֽׁאֲבֵי־ מַ֖יִם לְבֵ֥ית אֱלֹהָֽי׃

passages.text: The Gibeonites answered, “Your servants were told clearly that the LORD your God had commanded His servant Moses to give you all the land and wipe out all its inhabitants before you. So we greatly feared for our lives because of you, and that is why we have done this.
passages.sermon:
The Gibeonites spoke to Joshua.
They said, "We are your servants."
Someone told us what the LORD your God commanded Moses, His servant.
God commanded Moses to give you all this land.
God also commanded Moses to destroy all the people living in this land before you.
We heard this command.
We became very afraid for our lives because of you.
That is why we did this thing.
passages.original: וַיַּעֲנ֨וּ אֶת־ יְהוֹשֻׁ֜עַ וַיֹּאמְר֗וּ כִּי֩ הֻגֵּ֨ד הֻגַּ֤ד לַעֲבָדֶ֙יךָ֙ אֵת֩ אֲשֶׁ֨ר צִוָּ֜ה יְהוָ֤ה אֱלֹהֶ֙יךָ֙ אֶת־ מֹשֶׁ֣ה עַבְדּ֔וֹ לָתֵ֤ת לָכֶם֙ אֶת־ כָּל־ הָאָ֔רֶץ וּלְהַשְׁמִ֛יד אֶת־ כָּל־ יֹשְׁבֵ֥י הָאָ֖רֶץ מִפְּנֵיכֶ֑ם וַנִּירָ֨א מְאֹ֤ד לְנַפְשֹׁתֵ֙ינוּ֙ מִפְּנֵיכֶ֔ם וַֽנַּעֲשֵׂ֖ה אֶת־ הַדָּבָ֥ר הַזֶּֽה׃

passages.text: Now we are in your hands. Do to us whatever seems good and right to you.”
passages.sermon:
The Gibeonites spoke to Joshua.
They said, “We are now in your power.
You may decide what to do with us.
Do what is good in your eyes.
Do what is right in your eyes.
Treat us as you think best.”
passages.original: וְעַתָּ֖ה הִנְנ֣וּ בְיָדֶ֑ךָ כַּטּ֨וֹב וְכַיָּשָׁ֧ר בְּעֵינֶ֛יךָ לַעֲשׂ֥וֹת לָ֖נוּ עֲשֵֽׂה׃

passages.text: So Joshua did this and delivered them from the hands of the Israelites, and they did not kill the Gibeonites.
passages.sermon:
Joshua was the leader of Israel.
Joshua acted as he had promised the Gibeonites.
Joshua saved the Gibeonites from the Israelites.
The Israelites did not kill the Gibeonites.
passages.original: וַיַּ֥עַשׂ לָהֶ֖ם כֵּ֑ן וַיַּצֵּ֥ל אוֹתָ֛ם מִיַּ֥ד בְּנֵֽי־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל וְלֹ֥א הֲרָגֽוּם׃

passages.text: On that day he made them woodcutters and water carriers, as they are to this day for the congregation of the LORD and for the altar at the place He would choose.
passages.sermon:
Joshua was the leader of Israel.
On that day, Joshua gave the Gibeonites a new role.
He made the Gibeonites woodcutters.
He made the Gibeonites water carriers.
They served the congregation of the LORD.
They also served at the altar of the LORD.
They did this at the place the LORD would choose.
They continue in these roles to this day.
passages.original: וַיִּתְּנֵ֨ם יְהוֹשֻׁ֜עַ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא חֹטְבֵ֥י עֵצִ֛ים וְשֹׁ֥אֲבֵי מַ֖יִם לָֽעֵדָ֑ה וּלְמִזְבַּ֤ח יְהוָה֙ עַד־ הַיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֔ה אֶל־ הַמָּק֖וֹם אֲשֶׁ֥ר יִבְחָֽר׃פ
